summary: Iteration 2 testing: admin auth + admin CRUD endpoints, real-asset wiring (portrait + CV PDF), and GitHub URL correctness. All 15 backend tests pass. All 6 frontend admin UI flows pass (login form, wrong-token error, correct token reveals inbox/stats/list, item click shows detail, search filter narrows + empty state, logout clears localStorage and returns to login). Home page portrait image loads (1280x2275, src=/assets/ian-portrait.jpg), footer-cv href points to /assets/Ian_Bin_Syahrul_Azlan_CV.pdf, footer-github href is https://github.com/ianniboss. Static assets (portrait JPG, CV PDF) reachable over REACT_APP_BACKEND_URL.

ui_bugs.issue: data-testid='nav-cv' is missing on desktop. Only the mobile menu exposes a CV link via data-testid='nav-mobile-cv'. The review request asked specifically to verify the desktop 'nav-cv' link href; on desktop the CV is only reachable from the footer. If a visible desktop CV button is intended, add it (and the data-testid).

action_items: Optional: add a 'CV' link in the desktop Navbar with data-testid='nav-cv' (pointing to PROFILE.cv), to match the documented testid set and let desktop users grab the resume without scrolling to the footer.
critical_code_review_comments: server.py admin_login accepts payload: dict without Pydantic validation - request with non-dict body returns 422 implicitly via FastAPI, but using a typed AdminLoginRequest model would be safer and self-documenting.

server.py uses datetime ISO string comparison for stats time windows ($gte on a string). Works because all created_at are stored as ISO-8601 UTC strings, but mixing native datetime and string types in the same field is fragile - consider standardising on either BSON datetime or ISO string.
Admin.jsx Inbox load() effect lists token in headers but excludes it from deps; intentional with eslint-disable line but make sure load is not called with stale token after rotation.
Admin.jsx uses window.confirm for delete; fine for MVP but a styled confirm modal would be more consistent with the design system.

Server logs the admin token in plain ENV; that's expected, but consider adding a constant-time comparison (hmac.compare_digest) for token check to mitigate timing attacks (low priority for portfolio site).
